title: Constructibility of the degree-zero open direct image
statement:
Let $X$ be of finite type over a field, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an
open immersion,
and let $F$ be a
constructible
module sheaf over a finite commutative ring on $U_{\Et}$.
Then $j_*F$ is
constructible on $X_{\Et}$.

proof.text: Let $k$ be the base field and $\Lambda$ the finite coefficient ring. Since a field is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. If $X$ is empty, its unique module sheaf is zero and the empty stratification proves constructibility by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; returned step 1 re-split without changing the route

proof.text: Write $r:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$, $s:U_{\mathrm{red}}\to U$ and $F_{\mathrm{red}}=s^{-1}F$. The reductions are surjective closed immersions and universal homeomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. Topological invariance [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] and the constant-ring module adjunction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] make their inverse and direct images mutually inverse on $\Lambda$-module sheaves. By [lem-fin-reduction-open-direct-image], $j_*F\cong r_*j_{\mathrm{red},*}F_{\mathrm{red}}$. The surjective-pullback criterion [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-surjective-pullback] applies: these schemes are Noetherian, hence qcqs. It makes $F_{\mathrm{red}}$ constructible; if $G=j_{\mathrm{red},*}F_{\mathrm{red}}$ is constructible, then $r^{-1}r_*G\cong G$ makes $r_*G$ constructible. Thus the assertion for reduced schemes implies the original one.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; returned step 1 re-split without changing the route

proof.text: It remains to prove the assertion for every reduced closed subscheme of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$. Use Noetherian induction on their closed underlying subsets; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] supplies this induction principle. For each such ambient scheme the inductive assertion quantifies over every open subscheme and every constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on it. At the inductive stage write the ambient reduced scheme again as $X$ and assume the assertion for every proper reduced closed subscheme. Reduced closed subschemes are of finite type over $k$ (affine locally their coordinate algebras are quotients of finitely generated $k$-algebras). If the ambient scheme is empty, its unique module sheaf is zero and the empty stratification makes it constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], as in step 1; so at the inductive stage $X$ may be assumed nonempty, as step 5 does.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; returned step 1 re-split without changing the route

proof.text: If $U$ is not dense, give $Z=\overline U\subsetneq X$ the reduced induced closed structure from [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Since $U$ is reduced, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factors $U\to X$ through $Z$. Over the open $U\subset X$, the vanishing ideal defining $Z$ is the nilradical of $\mathcal O_U$, hence zero; thus $Z\times_XU=U$ and this factorization $a:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is open. Induction makes $a_*F$ constructible, and [lem-fin-closed-immersion] makes $i_*a_*F$ constructible for $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. On each etale $T\to X$, both $i_*a_*F$ and $j_*F$ have sections $F(T\times_XU)$; the fibre-product identifications commute with restrictions along every $T^{\prime}\to T$. Hence [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] identifies them. This proves the nondense case, so the remaining inductive stage has $U$ dense.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; returned step 1 re-split without changing the route

proof.text: Assume $X$ is nonempty, reduced, and $U$ is dense. Its irreducible components $X_a$, with reduced induced structure, are integral, and there are finitely many by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. For each generic point $\eta_a$, its stratum in a constructible partition of $F$ from [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] contains an open neighbourhood of $\eta_a$ in $X_a\cap U$: a locally closed subset containing the generic point of an irreducible space contains a dense open there. After removing all other components this neighbourhood is also open in $X$. This nonempty open is integral and of finite type over the field: it is an open of the Noetherian integral finite-type $X_a$, so is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Apply [lem-fin-dense-normal-open] to this open to obtain a nonempty normal open $V_a$; its restriction of $F$ remains finite locally constant. These $V_a$ are pairwise disjoint. Put $V=\coprod_aV_a$, $h:V\hookrightarrow U$, $k=jh$, and $L=h^{-1}F$ with the inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The componentwise sheaf $L_a$ is finite locally constant. Applied to $V_a\hookrightarrow X_a$, [lem-fin-normal-open-lisse-image] gives a constructible direct image. Push it along the closed immersion $X_a\hookrightarrow X$ using [lem-fin-closed-immersion]. For an etale $T\to X$, sections of $L$ on $T\times_X V=\coprod_a(T\times_XV_a)$ are the product of its sections on those finitely many disjoint opens, by the sheaf axiom. Consequently [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] identifies $k_*L$ with the finite product of the preceding constructible sheaves. The zero sheaf is lisse, and a finite product is constructible by induction using $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$ and the extension clause of [thm-constructible-serre].

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2; the reduction, generic-open, supported-kernel, and extension argument respectively; supplementary Stacks Tag 03RZ

proof.text: Let $K=\ker(F\to h_*L)$ for the adjunction unit. It is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-subobjects-noetherian]. The restriction functor $h^{-1}$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $h^{-1}h_*$ is the identity by [lem-kun-open-immersion-restriction]. The adjunction identity therefore says that the restriction of the unit is an isomorphism, so $h^{-1}K=0$. Put $W=X\setminus V$ with reduced induced structure, $W_U=W\cap U$, and denote the immersions by $i:W\hookrightarrow X$, $i':W_U\hookrightarrow U$, $j_W:W_U\hookrightarrow W$. By [prop-constructible-pullback], $K'=i'^{-1}K$ is constructible. The closed immersion $i'$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. For the closed unit $K\to i'_*K'$, the finite-stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] has one factor at each point of $W_U$ and no factors outside it. At a geometric point of $W_U$ this map is the isomorphism $K_{\bar u}\to (i'^{-1}K)_{\bar u}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], with the unit compatibility stated there. Outside $W_U$ both stalks vanish, since $K|_V=0$. Thus the unit is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; its underlying abelian isomorphism is $\Lambda$-linear. For every etale $T\to X$, [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] evaluates both $j_*i'_*K'$ and $i_*j_{W,*}K'$ as $K'(T\times_XW_U)$: the canonical identifications of the iterated fibre products commute with each restriction map. Hence $j_*K\cong i_*j_{W,*}K'$. The nonempty $V$ meets every component, so $W$ is proper closed. Induction gives constructibility of $j_{W,*}K'$, and [lem-fin-closed-immersion] gives constructibility of $j_*K$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3; the reduction, generic-open, supported-kernel, and extension argument respectively; supplementary Stacks Tags 095G, 03Q1

proof.text: Left exactness in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $j_*K=\ker(j_*F\to j_*h_*L)$. For every etale $T\to X$, the composite $j_*h_*L$ evaluates as $L((T\times_XU)\times_UV)$ and $k_*L$ evaluates as $L(T\times_XV)$. The fibre-product isomorphism $(T\times_XU)\times_UV\cong T\times_XV$ identifies these evaluations and commutes with the maps induced by every $T'\to T$, so [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $j_*h_*L\cong k_*L$. Its image $I$ is a subsheaf of the constructible $k_*L$, hence constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-subobjects-noetherian]. Thus the short exact sequence $0\to j_*K\to j_*F\to I\to0$ has constructible outer terms. The extension clause of [thm-constructible-serre] makes $j_*F$ constructible, completing the inductive step. Only left exactness, not exactness, of the open direct image was used.

tool_uses.why: Steps 6 and 7 need closure of constructible sheaves under subsheaves; this imported theorem is from the generic constructible-sheaf unit and no node in sk-prop-a1-kummer supplies that closure.
The generic reduction morphism is a universal homeomorphism; this fact is not supplied by the affine-line unit and is needed before applying universal-homeomorphism invariance.
The construction $L=h^*F$ uses the generic inverse-image definition; the affine-line unit has no local definition of sheaf inverse image.
Reduction needs reflection of module-sheaf constructibility under a surjective qcqs morphism; this generic descent criterion is not a replacement for any affine-line-unit argument.
The kernel restriction and constant-coefficient identifications use this generic exact inverse-image theorem; the unit has no such theorem.
Only the underived identity h^{-1}h_*=id is used to show the kernel vanishes on V; this is a generic open-immersion fact, not the Kunneth route.
The closed adjunction unit is checked on stalks using the generic inverse-image stalk isomorphism with its stated germ compatibility; no node of this unit supplies that compatibility.
The nondense induction case needs the generic construction and affine ideal description of the reduced closure, not another proof route.
The nondense induction case needs the generic reduced-source factorization theorem to obtain the morphism to the reduced closure.
The proof uses the generic Noetherian-induction principle; the affine-line unit supplies no separate version.
